Alex (Sales): quick sync — Acme POC going to execs tomorrow. Need final throughput-sizing recommendation, reserved-GPU ask, and any security questionnaire blockers. Can eng + security confirm?
Maya-SE: got it. What traffic mix are we planning? chat vs embeddings vs long-context generation?
Alex (Sales): mostly chat (histories ~1.5k tokens), some embeddings for search. Expected steady 40-60 rps; spikes to ~700 rps for 3-6m during promos. SLA goal: p95 < 400ms token latency.
Jon Eng: ok. For that profile I'd recommend: 4 reserved GPUs (A100-80 equiv) + autoscale pool for bursts. Key reasons: steady throughput covered by reserved, bursts handled by bounded autoscale to avoid cold starts. Also enable prefix/KV cache warmup for chat histories.
Maya-SE: can you sketch the autoscale policy we'll hand to infra?
Jon Eng: sure — pseudoconfig:```
min_gpu: 2
reserved_gpu: 4
burst_pool_max: 8
scale_up_trigger: gpu_util > 70% for 30s
scale_down_trigger: gpu_util < 30% for 60s
prewarm: true
kv_warm: enabled (prefix cache)
```
Maya-SE: nice. Any suggestion for prewarm/runbook to guarantee p95 during promo spikes?
Jon Eng: two things: 1) preheat KV cache before window (script below), 2) use prewarmed instances with instant attach for burst pool. Example warmup request:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/internal/warmup 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $WARMUP_TOKEN' 
 -d '{"model":"chat-3b-q4", "prompts": 200, "max_tokens": 1024}'
```
This primes KV and kernels so first-user requests hit cached states.
Sophie-Enablement: security checklist: Acme asked about KMS integration, SOC2 evidence, and VPC peering options. Also direct question: do reserved instances keep customer data isolated?
Jon Eng: yes — reserved pools are tenant-isolated compute; control plane still logs calls unless private deployment chosen. We'll provide KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and SOC2 reports. For VPC peering we need their infra contact to set up tunnels.
Alex (Sales): pricing / commercial Q: customer wants a blended rate for reserved + burst credits. Any quick numbers to share?
Maya-SE: rough ballpark: reserved GPU commit gives ~40% discount vs on-demand, burst credits billed at on-demand per-GPU-hour. Exact depends on model quantization (q4 vs fp16) and token profile. I'll pull numbers.
Jon Eng: also flag: if they want longer context or a larger model for quality, that increases GPU footprint; we should propose a QA run of 1-2 days of synthetic traffic to validate.
Alex (Sales): can you own the synthetic smoke test for Monday? Need sample load script and expected KPIs.
Jon Eng: yes — I'll push a small job into internal CI. CI Bot: deploy queued: smoke-test/acme-preheat-1734500000. Started 1734500200.
Maya-SE: items to collect from Acme: golden prompts for eval, expected peak window times, infra contact for VPC peering, and permissive test API keys for warmup.
Sophie-Enablement: I'll prepare security answers and attach SOC2 + KMS docs to the deal room.
Alex (Sales): perfect. Action items: @Jon Eng run synthetic smoke test Monday (owner), @Maya-SE finalize pricing ballpark and mapping to reserved+burst (owner), @Sophie-Enablement complete security Qs and share docs (owner). I'll update Acme and ask for infra contacts. :thumbsup:
Maya-SE: noted. Will add preheat credit ask to PO template.
Jon Eng: smoke test plan summary: 30m steady at 60 rps + 6x 5min spikes to 700 rps; verify p95 token latency < 400ms, no OOMs, KV hit-rate > 80%.
Alex (Sales): thanks team. If smoke test passes we include reserved 4 GPU commit + burst pool in SOW.
Sophie-Enablement: will also note fallback policy: if bursts exceed burst_pool_max, route to cheaper model variant for degraded but available service.
Alex (Sales): great — I'll close the loop with Acme after CI results.
Jon Eng: FYI if they insist on air-gapped/private deployment it's a different sizing path (on-prem capacity planning) — flag for later.
Alex (Sales): noted. End of thread.
